observation_summary: The system was throwing ClassCastException when using deep stubs because it was creating mocks using only the raw return type, ignoring generic type information and extra interfaces.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves rewriting the mock creation logic to properly account for generic metadata and extra interfaces. By introducing 'createNewDeepStubMock' and 'withSettingsUsing', the code now correctly configures the mock with the necessary type information, rather than just the raw class type. This is a procedural change to the algorithm used to generate deep stubs, fitting the Algorithm/Method category.
evidence_used: The fix introduces 'createNewDeepStubMock' and 'withSettingsUsing' to properly configure mocks with generic metadata.
The original code used 'invocation.getMethod().getReturnType()' which was insufficient for complex generic types.
The stack traces show ClassCastException, indicating that the created mock did not implement the expected interfaces or types.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix changes how mocks are configured, the root cause is the internal logic of how the deep stub mock is constructed (the algorithm), not a mismatch in an existing API contract between two components.
This is a refinement of an existing capability (deep stubbing) rather than the addition of a missing design-level feature.
